items.title: Japan to support infrastructure recovery in Gulf nations hit by Iran war
Has the U.S. lost its dominance to China?
items.description: Beijing may be benefiting from the war in Iran and Trump's tariffs and has an edge in the competition for tech supremacy. The New Yorker's Evan Osnos discusses his story "The Future, Made in China."

items.title: Netanyahu gave a ‘victory to Hamas’ by rejecting US-backed Gaza peace plan
items.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s rejection of a US-backed peace plan for Gaza last week offered a diplomatic victory to Hamas, according to some analysts. The Palestinian Islamist movement had agreed to gradually give up weapons in exchange for an Israeli withdrawal from Gaza, but agreeing on the definition …

items.title: Eurovision to exclude countries at war from hosting contest
items.description: The organizers of the song contest did not mention any country by name, but Israel came close to winning the competition in both 2025 and 2026, ultimately finishing second on each occasion. The organizers also announced an increase in the minimum age of competitors.

items.title: Due to the Iran war, Iraq is running out of money
items.description: Because of the blockage of the Strait of Hormuz, Iraq cannot export enough oil to fund the country's huge public sector. Protests have already started. Will the Iran war destabilize Iraq again?

items.title: Israeli settlers besieging Palestinian families in West Bank village
items.description: Israeli security forces have reportedly withdrawn and about a dozen settlers are said to remain at the site where two families have been besieged since Sunday.

items.title: Is Russia’s economy cracking despite the Iran war windfall?
items.description: A widening deficit and Ukrainian strikes are testing Russia's economy, even as war in the Middle East lifts oil revenue.

items.title: Deadly attack on Red Sea ship adds to global supply chain uncertainty
items.description: A strike on a merchant ship off the southern coast of Yemen that reportedly killed several seafarers on Tuesday threatens to reignite deep concerns about global trade, amid the ongoing Iran-US war that has choked shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Ukraine Repels 185 Combat Clashes on Tuesday
items.description: The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) reported 185 combat clashes over the past 24 hours, as Russian forces launched nearly 6,770 drones and 208 guided aerial bombs (KABs) nationwide.

items.title: In Ukraine, a city waits to rebuild a symbol of resistance
items.description: Instead of rushing to repair a war damaged university, policymakers decided to wait. They gained international support – and a new future.

items.title: One Killed in Ukrainian Attack on Wildberries Logistics Center in Voronezh
items.description: The online retailer said it evacuated employees from the facility after a fire broke out during the overnight drone strikes.

items.title: Russia Reports 13 Dead After Ukrainian Drones Strike In Tatarstan
items.description: Russia said at least 13 people, including a child, were killed in Ukrainian attacks on targets in the central region of Tatarstan, one of Kyiv's deadliest single attacks since the Kremlin launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine more than four years ago.
